text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak visits Luxor and says discoveries of iron ore deposits in the region will be a good opportunity for private investors. Mubarak inaugurates bridge on the Nile in Luxor which is hoped to facilitate the flow of tourism and economic growth.
- Mubarak receives invitation from Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati to attend the Organisation of Islamic Conference in Tehran in December.

- Egypt urges the United Nations committee charged with overseeing sanctions on Iraq to speed up its review and approval of contracts from countries which want to take part in the oil-for-food deal, so Iraq can buy food and medicine.
- Consultative council will discuss the 1997/98 budget from Saturday, after Mubarak passed it on to the council.
- Thursday is official holiday because of the first day of the Moslem Hijra calendar year.
- Mubarak will receive today the German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel.
- Social Fund for Development is studying finance for youth and family projects in Toshka as part of plans to develop the region.
- Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says the exercises between Turkey and Israel are a cause for concern if they are intended to be a message to Arabs and others.
- Agriculture Minister Youssef Wali said he expected the volume of investments in projects associated with Toshka to reach about 300 billion pounds.
- Mubarak will receive the Colombian president on Thursday.
